guide.name: Franklin Voter Guide
guide.note:
Written by the Franklin Civic Alliance. We interviewed every candidate who agreed to meet with
us and read every measure in full. Where a board member had a conflict, they did not
participate in that recommendation and we say so in the contest.

Always double check the options printed on your own ballot.

candidates.name: Dana Lombardi
candidates.note:
Appointed in January 2025 to fill the vacancy left by Senator Hale's resignation. Previously
Secretary of State of Franklin.

items.title: President and Vice President of the United States
items.subtitle: Vote for one ticket
items.note: The president and vice president run as a ticket. Your single vote elects both.

recommendation.justification:
Hana Nakamura's first term delivered the port funding Franklin has sought for a
decade. The challengers have not released a platform beyond a pledge to cut waste.

items.title: United States Senator (Special Election)
items.subtitle: Unexpired term ending January 3, 2027
items.note:
This is the first of two Senate contests on your ballot. This one decides who holds the
seat for the final weeks of the current term. Vote in both.

recommendation.justification:
See the full-term contest below. Our reasoning is the same, and splitting the vote
between the two contests would serve no purpose.

Dana Lombardi has used two years in the Senate to deliver the port funding Franklin
has sought for a decade. Sofia Yilmaz has not held office.

Odalys Halvorsen ran the department that this office oversees and left it in better
shape than they found it.

Bram Mendez is the only candidate who answered our questionnaire in full. The others
declined to meet with us.

Kiran Ueda has the clearest plan for the office and a record of delivering on it.
Elena Hossain has not said how the proposals would be paid for.

Wes Larsson has the clearest plan for the office and a record of delivering on it.
Nadia Okonkwo has not said how the proposals would be paid for.

Either is a fine choice. We did not reach consensus between them and would be happy
with both.

Rank Silas Osei first. Yusuf Eriksen is acceptable as a second choice; the rest of the
field is not ready for this office.

Rank Isaac Walsh first. Omar Chaudhry is acceptable as a second choice; the rest of
the field is not ready for this office.

Silas Reyes ran the department that this office oversees and left it in better shape
than they found it.

We endorsed Cedric Larsson last cycle and were disappointed. Tamsin Ivanova has spent
four years on the relevant commission and knows the budget line by line.

items.title: Supreme Court Justice
items.subtitle: Shall Justice Elena Villanueva be retained in office?

recommendation.justification:
Retention elections are not the place to relitigate a single decision. The bar
evaluation is "well qualified" and the opinions are careful.

items.title: Statewide Propositions
items.note:
Propositions 2 through 6 were placed by the legislature. Propositions 32 through 36 are
citizen initiatives.

items.title: Proposition 2
items.subtitle: Public school facilities bond
items.description:
Shall the measure titled "Public school facilities bond" be adopted, authorizing the
actions described in the full text and amending the relevant code sections accordingly?
items.if_yes: The public school facilities bond would take effect as described.
items.fiscal_impact: $300 per parcel per year for 30 years

recommendation.justification:
The existing subsidy is not enough and this modest increase is a cheap fix. It will
not solve the underlying shortage, but it is better than nothing.

items.title: Proposition 3
items.subtitle: Right to marry
items.fiscal_impact: $96 per parcel per year for 15 years

recommendation.justification:
This is a straightforward bond for infrastructure the district has deferred for a
decade. The repayment schedule is conservative and the oversight committee has real
teeth.

items.title: Proposition 32
items.subtitle: $18 minimum wage
items.fiscal_impact: Authorizes $96 million in bonds, repaid by property taxes over 30 years

recommendation.justification:
The mechanism here is the problem, not the goal. It sets no limits on what localities
may do in its place, and the cities most eager to use it have the worst records on the
underlying issue.

We would support a narrower version. Vote no on this one.
